subproblem.title: The integer-multiplicity action is continuous under uniform convergence on a compact set that carries the carrier
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), and let K ⊆ U be compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let h_j (j ∈ ℕ) and h be continuous maps ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with h_j → h uniformly on K. Then R.action(h_j) → R.action(h) as j → ∞, where R.action(g) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)) dHⁿ(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (hs : ℕ → Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (h : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ K) = 0 → (∀ j, Continuous (hs j)) → Continuous h → TendstoUniformlyOn hs h atTop K → Tendsto (fun j => R.action (hs j)) atTop (𝓝 (R.action h))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–6 of the parent proof (orientation bound, local integrability of θ on K, and the estimate |∫_M θξ(ω_j − h)| ≤ c·sup_K ‖ω_j − h‖). Here they are stated for an arbitrary triple R in U whose carrier lies in K up to an Hⁿ-null set, and for arbitrary continuous fields converging uniformly on K.
Notation. M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, Hⁿ := μHE[n], and μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. ‖·‖ is the operator norm of n-covectors. By definition, R.action(g) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫ θ·ξ(g) dμ.
1. μ-almost every point lies in K. M is measurable (R.measurableSet_carrier), so μ(ℝ^P ∖ K) = Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 by hypothesis. That is, x ∈ K for μ-a.e. x (ae_restrict_iff', ae_iff, measure_mono_null).
2. Orientation bound. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. So there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁,…,τₙ) such that either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for every n-covector α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for every α. Hence |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ‖τᵢ‖ = ‖α‖ for every α (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; ‖τᵢ‖ = 1 by orthonormality).
3. θ is μ-integrable. θ is measurable (R.measurable_mult) and nonnegative. By step 1, the sets M and M ∩ K differ by the Hⁿ-null set M ∖ K, while (M ∩ K) ∖ M = ∅. So μ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_congr_set). Then ∫θ dμ = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ (using ‖(m : ℝ)‖ₑ = m, Real.enorm_natCast), and this is finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set K ⊆ U. Put c := ∫θ dμ ∈ [0, ∞).
4. Measurability. For every continuous g : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P), the function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Indeed, θ is measurable, ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), g is continuous, and the evaluation map (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous.
5. Bounds and integrability. h is continuous and K is compact, so there is B with ‖h(x)‖ ≤ B for all x ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). By uniform convergence on K there is j₀ such that ‖h_j(x) − h(x)‖ < 1 for all j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ K; then ‖h_j(x)‖ ≤ B + 1 on K. Take j ≥ j₀ and a point x lying in K at which step 2 holds; by steps 1–2 this is μ-a.e. x. At such x, |θ(x)·ξ(x)(h_j(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖h_j(x)‖ ≤ (B + 1)·θ(x), and similarly |θ(x)·ξ(x)(h(x))| ≤ B·θ(x). By steps 3–4, the functions F_j := θ·ξ(h_j) (for j ≥ j₀) and F := θ·ξ(h) are therefore μ-integrable.
6. Convergence. Let ε > 0. By uniform convergence on K choose j₁ ≥ j₀ with ‖h_j(x) − h(x)‖ ≤ ε/(c + 1) for all j ≥ j₁ and x ∈ K. Fix j ≥ j₁. Both F_j and F are integrable, and ξ(x) is linear, so R.action(h_j) − R.action(h) = ∫ θ(x)·ξ(x)(h_j(x) − h(x)) dμ(x). Using step 2, and then step 1 (μ-a.e. x lies in K), |R.action(h_j) − R.action(h)| ≤ ∫ θ(x)·‖h_j(x) − h(x)‖ dμ(x) ≤ (ε/(c + 1))·c < ε. Hence R.action(h_j) → R.action(h).
Remark (equivalent formal route). Step 5 gives the bounds needed for dominated convergence, with dominating function (B + 1)·θ. Also F_j(x) → F(x) for every x ∈ K, because h_j(x) → h(x) and ξ(x) is a continuous linear functional. So tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence yields the same conclusion directly. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, so μ = Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in K. By R.orients (orthonormal τ, le_opNorm), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ μ-a.e.
μ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K), so θ is μ-integrable with c = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult on the compact K ⊆ U).
For continuous g, θ·ξ(g) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Bounds on K (‖h‖ ≤ B, eventually ‖h_j‖ ≤ B + 1) make θ·ξ(h_j) and θ·ξ(h) integrable.
|R.action(h_j) − R.action(h)| ≤ ∫ θ‖h_j − h‖ dμ ≤ c·sup_K‖h_j − h‖ → 0 (equivalently, dominated convergence with bound (B + 1)θ).

subproblem.title: Continuous compactly supported cut-off of the pulled-back form ω(f)∘Df that agrees with it on K
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open and K ⊆ O compact. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Let ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) be a continuous n-form (a continuous map into the n-covectors Covector (Euclid P) n). Then there is a continuous, compactly supported h : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) such that h(x) = ω(f(x))∘Df(x) for every x ∈ K. Here ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n), Continuous ω → IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → ∃ h : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, Continuous h ∧ HasCompactSupport h ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, h x = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof (continuity of γ = f^#ω on O, and the cutoff h = χγ). Here they are stated for an arbitrary continuous n-form ω. The parent applies this to its test form ω, which is C^∞ and hence continuous.
Notation. γ(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) for x ∈ ℝ^P. ‖·‖ denotes operator norms of n-covectors and of linear maps of ℝ^P.
1. f, Df and ω∘f are continuous on O. f is C¹ on the open set O, so f is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Its derivative Df = fderiv ℝ f is also continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, using 1 ≤ 1). Since ω is continuous, x ↦ ω(f(x)) is continuous on O.
2. Composition is jointly continuous. Let β, β' be n-covectors and A, A' linear maps of ℝ^P. Then β∘A − β'∘A' = (β − β')∘A + (β'∘A − β'∘A').
(a) ‖(β − β')∘A‖ ≤ ‖β − β'‖‖A‖ⁿ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le).
(b) Telescoping over the n slots gives (β'∘A − β'∘A')(v₁,…,vₙ) = Σ_{i=1}^{n} β'(A'v₁,…,A'v_{i−1},(A − A')vᵢ,Av_{i+1},…,Avₙ). Hence ‖β'∘A − β'∘A'‖ ≤ n‖β'‖·max(‖A‖,‖A'‖)^{n−1}·‖A − A'‖. For n = 0 the difference is 0.
Therefore (β, A) ↦ β∘A is continuous. In Mathlib: A ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM A is continuous into the continuous linear maps on covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM). Since β∘A = compContinuousLinearMapCLM A β, ContinuousOn.clm_apply gives continuity of x ↦ γ(x) on O from step 1.
3. By steps 1 and 2, γ is continuous on O.
4. Cutoff. ℝ^P is locally compact and Hausdorff, K ⊆ O is compact and O is open. So there is an open set V with K ⊆ V, closure V ⊆ O and closure V compact (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, which returns V, IsOpen V, K ⊆ V, closure V ⊆ O, IsCompact (closure V)). The compact set K and the closed set ℝ^P ∖ V are disjoint. Urysohn's lemma (exists_continuous_one_zero_of_isCompact) then gives a continuous χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with χ = 1 on K, χ = 0 on ℝ^P ∖ V, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, and compact support. The parent proof takes χ smooth; only continuity of χ is used here. Since χ vanishes outside V, supp χ ⊆ V, so tsupport χ ⊆ closure V ⊆ O.
5. Definition of h. Put h(x) := χ(x)·γ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. If x ∉ O then x ∉ tsupport χ, so χ(x) = 0 and h(x) = 0. Thus h is the parent's function: χγ on O and 0 off O.
6. h is continuous. On O, h is the product of the continuous function χ and the function γ, which is continuous on O by step 3; so h is continuous on O. Also supp h ⊆ supp χ, hence tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ O (tsupport_smul_subset_left). A function that is continuous on an open set containing its topological support is continuous (ContinuousOn.continuous_of_tsupport_subset): at x ∈ O use continuity on the open set O; at x ∉ tsupport h, h vanishes on a neighbourhood of x.
7. h has compact support: tsupport h is a closed subset of the compact set tsupport χ (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
8. For x ∈ K we have χ(x) = 1, so h(x) = γ(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x). By steps 6–8, h is continuous, compactly supported and equal to ω(f)∘Df on K. ∎
proof_key_steps: f and Df = fderiv ℝ f are continuous on the open set O (C¹), so x ↦ ω(f(x)) is continuous on O.
(β, A) ↦ β∘A is jointly continuous (telescoping estimate, or continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM with clm_apply), so γ = ω(f)∘Df is continuous on O.
Pick an open V with K ⊆ V and compact closure V ⊆ O. Urysohn then gives a continuous χ ∈ [0,1] with χ = 1 on K, χ = 0 off V and compact support, so tsupport χ ⊆ O.
h := χ·γ is continuous on O and tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ O, hence h is continuous. It has compact support and equals γ on K.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition matches every prose hypothesis and conclusion. The proof establishes pullback continuity using C¹ regularity on the open set, constructs the continuous cutoff with topological support inside O, and proves global continuity and compact support of its product with the pullback. Agreement on K suffices for the parent assembly. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and other children.

subproblem.title: Test forms approximate a continuous compactly supported covector field uniformly (mollification)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let h : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) be continuous with compact support. Here Λⁿ(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n, the n-covectors with the operator norm. Then there is a sequence (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} of test forms ω_j ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (elements of TestFormOn univ n, i.e. C^∞ n-forms with compact support) converging to h uniformly on ℝ^P: sup_x ‖ω_j(x) − h(x)‖ → 0 as j → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (h : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → ∃ ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, TendstoUniformly (fun j x => (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) h atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the mollifications ω_j := h ∗ ρ_j), applied to the continuous compactly supported field h.
Notation. E := Covector (Euclid P) n, the n-covectors of ℝ^P with the operator norm. volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^P.
1. Preliminaries. E is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence complete. h : ℝ^P → E is continuous with compact support. So h is locally integrable (Continuous.locallyIntegrable) and uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous).
2. Mollifiers. For j ∈ ℕ let r_j := 1/(j+1) > 0. Let φ_j be the smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius r_j/2 and outer radius r_j (a ContDiffBump). Then φ_j is C^∞, 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1, supp φ_j = ball(0, r_j), and φ_j has compact support. φ_j is nonnegative, continuous, integrable, and positive on the open ball ball(0, r_j), which has positive measure. Hence c_j := ∫φ_j > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, measure_ball_pos). Put ρ_j := φ_j / c_j. Then ρ_j is C^∞, ρ_j ≥ 0, supp ρ_j ⊆ supp φ_j = ball(0, r_j), ρ_j has compact support, and ∫ρ_j = 1 (integral_div). The normalisation is done by hand because ContDiffBump.normed is not imported by the frozen contract.
3. The test forms. Let ω_j := ρ_j ⋆ h, i.e. ω_j(x) = ∫ρ_j(t)·h(x − t) dt. This is the convolution with respect to scalar multiplication ℝ × E → E (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) and Lebesgue measure.
(a) ρ_j is C^∞ with compact support and h is locally integrable, so ω_j is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
(b) ρ_j and h have compact support, so ω_j has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution; supp ω_j ⊆ supp ρ_j + supp h).
Thus IsTestForm ω_j holds. Also tsupport ω_j ⊆ ℝ^P = univ trivially, so ω_j is an element of TestFormOn univ n.
4. Uniform estimate. Let ε > 0. By uniform continuity of h choose δ > 0 such that dist(h(y), h(x)) < ε/2 whenever dist(y, x) < δ. Choose J ∈ ℕ with 1/(J+1) < δ (exists_nat_one_div_lt). Let j ≥ J and x ∈ ℝ^P. Every y ∈ ball(x, r_j) satisfies dist(y, x) < r_j ≤ 1/(J+1) < δ, so dist(h(y), h(x)) ≤ ε/2. We have ρ_j ≥ 0, ∫ρ_j = 1 and supp ρ_j ⊆ ball(0, r_j). Hence ω_j(x) − h(x) = ∫ρ_j(t)·(h(x − t) − h(x)) dt, and therefore ‖ω_j(x) − h(x)‖ ≤ ∫ρ_j(t)·‖h(x − t) − h(x)‖ dt ≤ ε/2 (dist_convolution_le, with radius r_j, bound ε/2 and centre value h(x)).
5. Conclusion. For all j ≥ J and all x ∈ ℝ^P, dist(h(x), ω_j(x)) ≤ ε/2 < ε. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, ω_j → h uniformly on ℝ^P (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff; the uniform structure on E is the one induced by its norm). ∎
proof_key_steps: Covector (Euclid P) n is a complete normed space; h is locally integrable and uniformly continuous.
Normalised smooth bumps ρ_j = φ_j/∫φ_j satisfy ρ_j ≥ 0, ∫ρ_j = 1 and supp ρ_j ⊆ ball(0, 1/(j+1)).
ω_j := ρ_j ⋆ h (lsmul convolution) is C^∞ with compact support, so ω_j ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
By uniform continuity and dist_convolution_le, sup_x ‖ω_j(x) − h(x)‖ ≤ ε/2 for j ≥ J. Hence TendstoUniformly.

audit.reason: The exact type expresses the claimed uniform approximation in operator norm. The supplied proof verifies positive finite bump normalization, smoothness and compact support of scalar convolution, and an epsilon estimate uniform in x. Completeness and the norm-induced uniform structure were independently checked in Lean. No missing hypothesis or circular dependency is present.
